item.title: Review File Versions on Mac with Compare Files Viewer
item.description:
Compare Files Viewer is a native Mac app for reviewing file-comparison results produced by a Shortcut or another tool.

A folder full of “final”, “final-2”, and “final-revised” files creates two questions: how are they related, and which version should you open first? A readable comparison report can help, especially when its conclusion is accompanied by paths, dates, hashes, or text differences.

Compare Files Viewer provides that presentation layer. It does not compare files itself. Another producer must inspect the files and send a result payload.

Updated interface

Figure 1 shows the exact-match sample with the Liquid Glass action bar. The sample uses demonstration paths and abbreviated hashes.

Figure 2 shows the Details sheet, including file groups, metadata, and local evidence.

Build the viewer

The project requires macOS 26 or later and Xcode/Command Line Tools with a compatible SDK. Source builds and an importable Shortcut are available; there is currently no packaged GitHub Release app.

Download the source and build from its root:

1

bash scripts/build-app.sh

The app is built at .build/CompareFilesViewer.app. Create ~/Applications and copy the app there, or install it in /Applications. The Shortcut checks these locations in that order without a personal username. To inspect an example with the built executable:

1

.build/CompareFilesViewer.app/Contents/MacOS/CompareFilesViewer --file ExamplePayload.json

Example paths may not exist on your Mac. The sample demonstrates the report format rather than comparing your own documents.

On your first look, start with the proposed main version and version order, then open Details to see the evidence behind that suggestion. This lets you understand the window before deciding whether to connect your own comparison workflow. The sample does not read any “final” files in your folder.

What a report can show

The payload contains files, analysis, and optional local_evidence. Depending on the producer, the viewer can display:

  • The overall relationship and confidence.
  • A recommended main version and proposed version order.
  • Finder icons, paths, file sizes, and modification times.
  • Local SHA-256 metadata, text differences, or image-comparison evidence.

A Details sheet and Reveal in Finder actions make it easier to investigate the reasoning. English and Simplified Chinese interfaces are supported.

The usefulness of those fields depends on the upstream comparison. A missing hash is not proof of difference; an AI-generated grouping is not the same as byte-for-byte equality.

Imagine two reports that differ by one number. The newer modification date tells you which one to open first, but the actual difference and the files’ origins decide which to keep. If the producer supplied only dates, the viewer cannot invent a text diff or hash as missing evidence.

Connect your own producer

The app accepts a JSON file through --file, JSON text through --json, or a payload on stdin. Use ExamplePayload.json as the schema reference when writing a Shortcut or script.

The repository now includes an importable Compare Files.shortcut. Download the raw file and double-click to import it. If a shortcut with that name already exists, manually remove the old copy in Shortcuts first; leave your source files intact.

Allow running scripts in Shortcuts settings and inspect the Use Model action. It defaults to ChatGPT and requires an available model/account configured on the device. The Language Text action defaults to $language$ == English; change it to $language$ == Simplified Chinese if preferred. Select at least two files in Finder and choose Quick Actions → Compare Files. Enable the Quick Action in System Settings if it is missing.

Both shell actions use /bin/zsh and pass input as arguments. The first receives the selected files. The final action receives a list with local JSON first and, only when needed, the model’s JSON second. Preserve this order.

Local ERROR results display an error; LOCAL_RESULT opens the viewer directly; only AI_REQUIRED calls the model. Model input includes names, paths, metadata, text excerpts and local comparison evidence, not just hashes. Check your selected model’s data handling before use. The viewer itself makes no network requests.

This is therefore most useful if you already have a comparison workflow and want a clearer native result window.

Read the sample as a worked example

The repository groups report.pdf, report-v2.pdf, and report-final.pdf. It proposes a main version and an order, with explanations such as an added chapter and changed page count. Start by checking whether the files belong to the same subject, then examine what changed. The word “final” is a useful label, not evidence on its own.

Open Details and compare paths, sizes, and modification times. A “final” copy in Downloads may be an older attachment resent by a colleague. A cloud-folder copy may contain comments that never reached the main draft. Paths explain where material came from; differences explain what it contains. Both matter when deciding what to keep.

The example uses demonstration paths and abbreviated hash values. It helps you understand the interface; it cannot establish anything about files on your Mac. Replacing a sample filename only edits the report. It does not ask the viewer to analyze the newly named document.

Understand the different kinds of evidence

A complete file hash can establish byte equality. A text hash concerns extracted text, which is a narrower question. Two PDFs can contain the same text while differing in layout, annotations, or embedded images. Decide whether your task concerns the words or the whole document before treating a text match as sufficient.

Text differences may also be excerpts. The sample records added and removed line counts, a few example lines, and a flag showing that samples were truncated. Use those excerpts to locate changes, then inspect the original context. A changed number means little until you know whether it is a price, date, reference, or page number.

The main-version recommendation helps set a reading order. It need not collapse every useful file into one survivor. An editable source, an annotated review copy, and a PDF prepared for sending can serve different purposes. Keeping those roles clear can be more useful than naming one universal “best” version.

Connect a producer through a saved report first

For your first integration, let the producer save a JSON file and open it with --file. This separates the analysis from display: if something looks wrong, you can inspect the input without debugging both stages at once. Move to a stdin pipeline only after the saved-file workflow works reliably.

Follow ExamplePayload.json: files describes the items, analysis holds relationships and recommendations, and local_evidence carries evidence actually collected. Leave unavailable evidence absent rather than inventing plausible explanations. Use real source paths so Reveal in Finder can take you to the documents.

If the viewer reports a loading or parsing error, check that the report file exists, contains valid JSON, and follows the expected structure. Distinguish the path supplied to --file from the document paths inside that file. One opens the report; the others locate the compared material. Both layers must be correct for the handoff to be useful.

Decide what “main version” really means

Modification time alone does not establish the best version. Copying and exporting can change dates, while two documents can differ in small but important edits. Treat the recommendation as a place to start reviewing.

Open the proposed main file, verify the differences that matter, and retain originals until you have confirmed the relationship. The viewer does not merge documents or provide a reason to delete alternatives automatically.

The app itself makes no network requests and does not upload selected files. Privacy and AI policies belong to the producer that generated the payload.

For first understanding an unfamiliar format, see What File Is This. For consistent names after the review, Auto Filename Helper is a separate workflow. The README and example payload are the starting point for integration.

These are the two scripts and full prompt used by the public Shortcut. Default paths work with each user’s own home directory. Standalone downloads are also provided below. The reviewable workflow XML is in Shortcut/Compare Files.xml in the repository.

# ============================================================
# Compare Files — Local Analyzer
#
# Output ALWAYS JSON:
#
# status = ERROR
#
# status = LOCAL_RESULT
#
# status = AI_REQUIRED
#
# ============================================================


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# JSON helpers
# ------------------------------------------------------------

json_string() {
    /usr/bin/printf '%s' "${1-}" |
    /usr/bin/perl \
        -MJSON::PP \
        -MEncode \
        -0777 \
        -e '
            use strict;
            use warnings;

            binmode STDIN, ":raw";
            binmode STDOUT, ":raw";

            local $/;
            my $raw = <STDIN>;
            $raw = "" unless defined $raw;

            my $text;

            eval {
                $text = Encode::decode(
                    "UTF-8",
                    $raw,
                    Encode::FB_CROAK
                );
            };

            if ($@) {
                $text = Encode::decode(
                    "UTF-8",
                    $raw,
                    Encode::FB_DEFAULT
                );
            }

            print JSON::PP
                ->new
                ->utf8
                ->allow_nonref
                ->encode($text);
        '
}


json_nullable_string() {
    local value="${1-}"

    if [[ -n "$value" && "$value" != "(null)" ]]; then
        json_string "$value"
    else
        print -rn -- "null"
    fi
}


json_number_or_null() {
    local value="${1-}"

    if [[ "$value" == <-> ]]; then
        print -rn -- "$value"
    else
        print -rn -- "null"
    fi
}


emit_simple_error() {
    local message="${1-Unknown error}"

    print -rn -- '{"schema_version":1,"status":"ERROR","error":'
    json_string "$message"
    print -r -- '}'
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Input validation
# ------------------------------------------------------------

if (( $# < 2 )); then
    emit_simple_error \
        "Please select at least 2 files in Finder before running Compare Files."
    exit 0
fi


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Temporary workspace
# ------------------------------------------------------------

TMPBASE="${TMPDIR:-/tmp/}"
[[ "$TMPBASE" == */ ]] || TMPBASE="${TMPBASE}/"

WORKDIR_CF="$(
    /usr/bin/mktemp \
        -d \
        "${TMPBASE}CompareFiles.XXXXXX"
)" || {
    emit_simple_error \
        "Unable to create the Compare Files temporary directory."
    exit 0
}


cleanup() {
    /bin/rm -rf "$WORKDIR_CF" 2>/dev/null || true
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ------------------------------------------------------------

lower() {
    print -r -- "$1" |
    /usr/bin/tr \
        '[:upper:]' \
        '[:lower:]'
}


normalize_family() {
    local n="$1"

    n="${n%.*}"

    print -r -- "$n" |
    /usr/bin/perl \
        -CSDA \
        -pe '
            for (1..4) {

                s/\s*\(\d+\)\s*$//;

                s/[\s._-]+(?:
                    copy|
                    duplicate|
                    backup|
                    bak|
                    new|
                    latest|
                    final(?:[-_ ]*final)?\d*|
                    rev(?:ision)?[-_ ]*\d+|
                    ver(?:sion)?[-_ ]*\d+|
                    v\d+(?:\.\d+)*|
                    副本|
                    复制|
                    备份|
                    最新版|
                    最终版|
                    定稿|
                    修订版\d*
                )\s*$//ix;

                s/[\s._-]+20\d{2}[-.]?\d{1,2}[-.]?\d{1,2}\s*$//;
            }

            s/[\s._-]+$//;
        ' |
    /usr/bin/tr \
        '[:upper:]' \
        '[:lower:]'
}


extract_text() {
    local f="$1"
    local ext="$2"
    local out="$3"

    : > "$out"

    case "$ext" in

        txt|md|markdown|csv|tsv|json|xml|html|htm|log)

            /bin/cat \
                "$f" \
                2>/dev/null \
                > "$out" \
                || true
            ;;


        rtf|rtfd|doc|docx|odt|pages)

            if [[ -x /usr/bin/textutil ]]; then

                /usr/bin/textutil \
                    -convert txt \
                    -stdout \
                    "$f" \
                    2>/dev/null \
                    > "$out" \
                    || true

            fi
            ;;


        pdf)

            /usr/bin/mdls \
                -raw \
                -name kMDItemTextContent \
                "$f" \
                2>/dev/null |
            /usr/bin/sed \
                '/^(null)$/d' \
                > "$out" \
                || true
            ;;


        pptx|ppsx)

            if [[ -x /usr/bin/unzip ]]; then

                /usr/bin/unzip \
                    -p \
                    "$f" \
                    'ppt/slides/slide*.xml' \
                    2>/dev/null |
                /usr/bin/perl \
                    -CSDA \
                    -pe '
                        s#</a:p>#\n#g;
                        s#<[^>]+># #g;
                        s/&/&/g;
                        s/</</g;
                        s/>/>/g;
                        s/"/"/g;
                        s/'/'"'"'/g;
                        s/[ \t\r]+/ /g;
                    ' \
                    > "$out" \
                    || true

            fi
            ;;


        xlsx|xlsm)

            if [[ -x /usr/bin/unzip ]]; then

                /usr/bin/unzip \
                    -p \
                    "$f" \
                    'xl/sharedStrings.xml' \
                    2>/dev/null |
                /usr/bin/perl \
                    -CSDA \
                    -pe '
                        s#</t>#\n#g;
                        s#<[^>]+># #g;
                        s/&/&/g;
                        s/</</g;
                        s/>/>/g;
                        s/"/"/g;
                        s/'/'"'"'/g;
                        s/[ \t\r]+/ /g;
                    ' \
                    > "$out" \
                    || true

            fi
            ;;


        *)

            /usr/bin/mdls \
                -raw \
                -name kMDItemTextContent \
                "$f" \
                2>/dev/null |
            /usr/bin/sed \
                '/^(null)$/d' \
                > "$out" \
                || true
            ;;
    esac
}


prepare_diff_text() {
    local input="$1"
    local output="$2"

    if [[ ! -s "$input" ]]; then
        : > "$output"
        return
    fi

    /usr/bin/perl \
        -CSDA \
        -pe '
            s/\r$//;
            s/[ \t]+$//;
        ' \
        "$input" \
        > "$output" \
        2>/dev/null \
        || true
}


truncate_diff_line() {
    /usr/bin/printf '%s' "${1-}" |
    /usr/bin/perl \
        -MEncode \
        -0777 \
        -e '
            use strict;
            use warnings;

            binmode STDIN, ":raw";
            binmode STDOUT, ":raw";

            local $/;
            my $raw = <STDIN>;
            $raw = "" unless defined $raw;

            my $text = Encode::decode(
                "UTF-8",
                $raw,
                Encode::FB_DEFAULT
            );

            $text =~ s/[ \t]+/ /g;

            if (length($text) > 400) {
                $text = substr($text, 0, 400) . "…";
            }

            print Encode::encode("UTF-8", $text);
        '
}


emit_sample_lines_json() {
    local file="$1"
    integer max_lines="${2:-6}"
    integer n=0
    integer first=1
    local line=""
    local shortened=""

    print -rn -- '['

    while IFS= read -r line || [[ -n "$line" ]]; do

        (( ++n ))

        if (( n > max_lines )); then
            break
        fi

        shortened="$(
            truncate_diff_line "$line"
        )"

        if (( ! first )); then
            print -rn -- ','
        fi

        first=0

        json_string "$shortened"

    done < "$file"

    print -rn -- ']'
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Read selected files

for f in "$@"; do

    (( ++idx ))

    paths[$idx]="$f"
    names[$idx]="${f:t}"


    if [[ ! -e "$f" ]]; then

        emit_simple_error \
            "Unable to read file: ${names[$idx]}. The file does not exist or has been moved."

        exit 0
    fi


    if [[ ! -f "$f" ]]; then

        emit_simple_error \
            "Folder comparison is not currently supported: ${names[$idx]}."

        exit 0
    fi


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Basic metadata
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    local_ext="${f:e}"

    exts[$idx]="$(
        lower "$local_ext"
    )"


    sizes[$idx]="$(
        /usr/bin/stat \
            -f '%z' \
            "$f" \
            2>/dev/null \
            || true
    )"


    created[$idx]="$(
        /usr/bin/mdls \
            -raw \
            -name kMDItemFSCreationDate \
            "$f" \
            2>/dev/null |
        /usr/bin/sed \
            -E \
            '
                /^(null)$/d
                s/ \+0000$//
            ' \
            || true
    )"


    modified[$idx]="$(
        /usr/bin/stat \
            -f '%Sm' \
            -t '%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z' \
            "$f" \
            2>/dev/null \
            || true
    )"


    hashes[$idx]="$(
        /usr/bin/shasum \
            -a 256 \
            "$f" \
            2>/dev/null |
        /usr/bin/awk \
            '{print $1}'
    )"


    if [[ -z "${hashes[$idx]}" ]]; then

        emit_simple_error \
            "Unable to calculate SHA-256 for file: ${names[$idx]}."

        exit 0
    fi


    families[$idx]="$(
        normalize_family \
            "${names[$idx]}"
    )"


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Extract text
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    tf="$WORKDIR_CF/text-$idx.txt"

    extract_text \
        "$f" \
        "${exts[$idx]}" \
        "$tf"

    text_files[$idx]="$tf"


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Prepare normalized text for line diff
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    dtf="$WORKDIR_CF/diff-text-$idx.txt"

    prepare_diff_text \
        "$tf" \
        "$dtf"

    diff_text_files[$idx]="$dtf"


    if [[ -s "$tf" ]]; then

        text_bytes[$idx]="$(
            /usr/bin/stat \
                -f '%z' \
                "$tf" \
                2>/dev/null \
                || print -r -- "0"
        )"


        # Complete extracted text signature.
        #
        # Whitespace is normalized, but CASE IS PRESERVED.
        # This means case changes are also detected.
        text_sigs[$idx]="$(
            /usr/bin/tr \
                -s \
                '[:space:]' \
                ' ' \
                < "$tf" |
            /usr/bin/shasum \
                -a 256 |
            /usr/bin/awk \
                '{print $1}'
        )"

    else

        text_bytes[$idx]="0"
        text_sigs[$idx]=""

    fi


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Media metadata
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    case "${exts[$idx]}" in

        jpg|jpeg|png|heic|heif|tif|tiff|gif|bmp|webp)

            image_indices+=("$idx")


            w="$(
                /usr/bin/sips \
                    -g pixelWidth \
                    "$f" \
                    2>/dev/null |
                /usr/bin/awk \
                    '/pixelWidth:/{print $2}'
            )"


            h="$(
                /usr/bin/sips \
                    -g pixelHeight \
                    "$f" \
                    2>/dev/null |
                /usr/bin/awk \
                    '/pixelHeight:/{print $2}'
            )"


            fmt="$(
                /usr/bin/sips \
                    -g format \
                    "$f" \
                    2>/dev/null |
                /usr/bin/awk \
                    '/format:/{print $2}'
            )"


            media_info[$idx]="Image ${w:-?}×${h:-?}, format ${fmt:-${exts[$idx]}}"
            ;;


        *)

            pages="$(
                /usr/bin/mdls \
                    -raw \
                    -name kMDItemNumberOfPages \
                    "$f" \
                    2>/dev/null |
                /usr/bin/sed \
                    '/^(null)$/d'
            )"


            ctype="$(
                /usr/bin/mdls \
                    -raw \
                    -name kMDItemContentType \
                    "$f" \
                    2>/dev/null |
                /usr/bin/sed \
                    '/^(null)$/d'
            )"


            if [[ -n "$pages" ]]; then

                media_info[$idx]="${ctype:-${exts[$idx]}}, pages ${pages}"

            else

                media_info[$idx]="${ctype:-${exts[$idx]}}"

            fi
            ;;
    esac

done


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Exact duplicate fast path

integer all_same=1

for (( i=2; i<=idx; i++ )); do

    if [[ "${hashes[$i]}" != "${hashes[1]}" ]]; then

        all_same=0
        break

    fi

done


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Image similarity evidence
# ------------------------------------------------------------

if (( ! all_same && ${#image_indices[@]} >= 2 )); then

    integer pair_count=0


    for (( a=1; a<=${#image_indices[@]}; a++ )); do

        i=${image_indices[$a]}


        for (( b=a+1; b<=${#image_indices[@]}; b++ )); do

            j=${image_indices[$b]}

            (( ++pair_count ))


            if (( pair_count > 30 )); then

                image_pair_limit_reached=1
                break 2

            fi


            bmp1="$WORKDIR_CF/image-$i.bmp"
            bmp2="$WORKDIR_CF/image-$j.bmp"


            if [[ ! -f "$bmp1" ]]; then

                /usr/bin/sips \
                    -z 64 64 \
                    -s format bmp \
                    "${paths[$i]}" \
                    --out "$bmp1" \
                    >/dev/null 2>&1 \
                    || true

            fi


            if [[ ! -f "$bmp2" ]]; then

                /usr/bin/sips \
                    -z 64 64 \
                    -s format bmp \
                    "${paths[$j]}" \
                    --out "$bmp2" \
                    >/dev/null 2>&1 \
                    || true

            fi


            score=""


            if [[ -s "$bmp1" && -s "$bmp2" ]]; then

                od1="$WORKDIR_CF/od-$i.txt"
                od2="$WORKDIR_CF/od-$j.txt"


                /usr/bin/tail \
                    -c +55 \
                    "$bmp1" |
                /usr/bin/od \
                    -An \
                    -tu1 \
                    -v |
                /usr/bin/tr \
                    -s \
                    ' ' \
                    '\n' |
                /usr/bin/sed \
                    '/^$/d' \
                    > "$od1"


                /usr/bin/tail \
                    -c +55 \
                    "$bmp2" |
                /usr/bin/od \
                    -An \
                    -tu1 \
                    -v |
                /usr/bin/tr \
                    -s \
                    ' ' \
                    '\n' |
                /usr/bin/sed \
                    '/^$/d' \
                    > "$od2"


                score="$(
                    /usr/bin/paste \
                        "$od1" \
                        "$od2" |
                    /usr/bin/awk '
                        NF == 2 {

                            d = $1 - $2

                            if (d < 0)
                                d = -d

                            total += d
                            count++
                        }

                        END {

                            if (count > 0)
                                printf "%.5f", total / (count * 255)
                        }
                    '
                )"

            fi


            image_pair_a+=("$i")
            image_pair_b+=("$j")
            image_pair_scores+=("${score:-null}")

        done
    done
fi

emit_files_json() {

            )"

        fi


        print -rn -- '{'

        print -rn -- ',"modified":'

        print -rn -- ',"sha256":'
        json_string "${hashes[$i]}"


        print -rn -- ',"text_sha256":'

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# JSON: pairwise text differences
# ------------------------------------------------------------

emit_text_differences_json() {

    print -rn -- '['

    integer pair_count=0
    integer output_count=0

    text_pair_limit_reached=0


    for (( i=1; i<=idx; i++ )); do

        for (( j=i+1; j<=idx; j++ )); do

            (( ++pair_count ))


            if (( pair_count > 30 )); then

                text_pair_limit_reached=1
                break 2

            fi


            (( ++output_count ))

            if (( output_count > 1 )); then
                print -rn -- ','
            fi


            print -rn -- '{'


            print -rn -- '"file_a":'
            json_string "${names[$i]}"


            print -rn -- ',"file_b":'
            json_string "${names[$j]}"


            # ------------------------------------------------
            # Text unavailable
            # ------------------------------------------------

            if [[ -z "${text_sigs[$i]}" ||
                  -z "${text_sigs[$j]}" ]]; then

                print -rn -- ',"status":"UNAVAILABLE"'
                print -rn -- ',"hunks":null'
                print -rn -- ',"added_lines":null'
                print -rn -- ',"removed_lines":null'
                print -rn -- ',"sample_added":[]'
                print -rn -- ',"sample_removed":[]'
                print -rn -- ',"samples_truncated":false'

                print -rn -- '}'
                continue
            fi


            # ------------------------------------------------
            # Extracted text identical
            # ------------------------------------------------

            if [[ "${text_sigs[$i]}" == "${text_sigs[$j]}" ]]; then

                print -rn -- ',"status":"IDENTICAL_TEXT"'
                print -rn -- ',"hunks":0'
                print -rn -- ',"added_lines":0'
                print -rn -- ',"removed_lines":0'
                print -rn -- ',"sample_added":[]'
                print -rn -- ',"sample_removed":[]'
                print -rn -- ',"samples_truncated":false'

                print -rn -- '}'
                continue
            fi


            # ------------------------------------------------
            # Calculate complete line diff
            #
            # Direction:
            # file_a -> file_b
            #
            # + = present in file_b, absent from file_a
            # - = present in file_a, absent from file_b
            # ------------------------------------------------

            diff_file="$WORKDIR_CF/diff-$i-$j.txt"
            added_file="$WORKDIR_CF/added-$i-$j.txt"
            removed_file="$WORKDIR_CF/removed-$i-$j.txt"

            : > "$added_file"
            : > "$removed_file"


            /usr/bin/diff \
                -U 0 \
                -- \
                "${diff_text_files[$i]}" \
                "${diff_text_files[$j]}" \
                > "$diff_file" \
                2>/dev/null \
                || true


            /usr/bin/awk \
                -v added="$added_file" \
                -v removed="$removed_file" \
                '
                    /^\+\+\+ / {
                        next
                    }

                    /^--- / {
                        next
                    }

                    /^\+/ {
                        print substr($0, 2) >> added
                        next
                    }

                    /^-/ {
                        print substr($0, 2) >> removed
                        next
                    }
                ' \
                "$diff_file"


            added_count="$(
                /usr/bin/wc \
                    -l \
                    < "$added_file" |
                /usr/bin/tr \
                    -d \
                    ' '
            )"


            removed_count="$(
                /usr/bin/wc \
                    -l \
                    < "$removed_file" |
                /usr/bin/tr \
                    -d \
                    ' '
            )"


            hunk_count="$(
                /usr/bin/grep \
                    -c \
                    '^@@' \
                    "$diff_file" \
                    2>/dev/null \
                    || true
            )"

            [[ -n "$hunk_count" ]] || hunk_count=0


            integer samples_truncated=0

            if (( ${added_count:-0} > 6 ||
                  ${removed_count:-0} > 6 )); then

                samples_truncated=1

            fi


            print -rn -- ',"status":"DIFFERENT_TEXT"'


            print -rn -- ',"hunks":'
            print -rn -- "${hunk_count:-0}"


            print -rn -- ',"added_lines":'
            print -rn -- "${added_count:-0}"


            print -rn -- ',"removed_lines":'
            print -rn -- "${removed_count:-0}"


            print -rn -- ',"sample_added":'
            emit_sample_lines_json \
                "$added_file" \
                6


            print -rn -- ',"sample_removed":'
            emit_sample_lines_json \
                "$removed_file" \
                6


            print -rn -- ',"samples_truncated":'

            if (( samples_truncated )); then
                print -rn -- 'true'
            else
                print -rn -- 'false'
            fi


            print -rn -- '}'

        done
    done


    print -rn -- ']'
}


# ------------------------------------------------------------
# JSON: local evidence

emit_local_evidence_json() {

    print -rn -- '{'


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Relation signals
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    print -rn -- '"relation_signals":['

    integer signal_count=0


    for (( i=1; i<=idx; i++ )); do

        for (( j=i+1; j<=idx; j++ )); do

            typeset -a flags
            flags=()


            if [[ "${hashes[$i]}" == "${hashes[$j]}" ]]; then

                flags+=("EXACT_SHA_MATCH")

            fi


            if [[ -n "${text_sigs[$i]}" &&
                  -n "${text_sigs[$j]}" ]]; then

                if [[ "${text_sigs[$i]}" == "${text_sigs[$j]}" ]]; then

                    flags+=("EXTRACTED_TEXT_MATCH")

                else

                    flags+=("EXTRACTED_TEXT_DIFFERS")

                fi

            fi


            if [[ -n "${families[$i]}" &&
                  "${families[$i]}" == "${families[$j]}" ]]; then

                flags+=("NORMALIZED_NAME_MATCH")

            fi


            if (( ${#flags[@]} > 0 )); then

                (( ++signal_count ))


                if (( signal_count > 1 )); then
                    print -rn -- ','
                fi


                signal="${names[$i]} ↔ ${names[$j]} : ${(j:, :)flags}"

                json_string "$signal"

            fi

        done
    done


    print -rn -- ']'


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Complete extracted-text differences
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    print -rn -- ',"text_differences":'

    emit_text_differences_json


    print -rn -- ',"text_pair_limit_reached":'

    if (( text_pair_limit_reached )); then
        print -rn -- 'true'
    else
        print -rn -- 'false'
    fi


    # --------------------------------------------------------
    # Image differences
    # --------------------------------------------------------

    print -rn -- ',"image_differences":['

    integer image_result_count=${#image_pair_a[@]}


    for (( p=1; p<=image_result_count; p++ )); do

        if (( p > 1 )); then
            print -rn -- ','
        fi


        i=${image_pair_a[$p]}
        j=${image_pair_b[$p]}
        score="${image_pair_scores[$p]}"


        print -rn -- '{'


        print -rn -- '"file_a":'
        json_string "${names[$i]}"


        print -rn -- ',"file_b":'
        json_string "${names[$j]}"


        print -rn -- ',"score":'

        if [[ "$score" == "null" || -z "$score" ]]; then

            print -rn -- 'null'

        else

            print -rn -- "$score"

        fi


        print -rn -- '}'

    done


    print -rn -- ']'


    print -rn -- ',"image_pair_limit_reached":'

    if (( image_pair_limit_reached )); then
        print -rn -- 'true'
    else
        print -rn -- 'false'
    fi


    print -rn -- '}'
}

For example:

report.pdf
report (1).pdf
report-v2.pdf
report-final.pdf

may produce the same normalized_family.

This may only be used as supporting evidence that the files may belong to the same file family.

It cannot independently prove that:

- the file contents are identical
- the files are different versions
- the version order
- which file is newer


6. path

path is mainly used to distinguish files stored in different locations.

You must not infer from directory names or paths alone:

- version order
- content relationships
- which file is more important
- which file should be treated as the main version


7. created / modified

Creation and modification timestamps may only be used as supporting evidence.

You must not determine solely from created or modified:

- which version is newer
- which file should be treated as the main version

Possible reasons include:

- copying a file may change timestamps
- downloading may change timestamps
- exporting may change timestamps
- cloud synchronization may change timestamps


====================
3. INTERPRETING TEXT DIFFS
====================

local_evidence.text_differences contains local pairwise line-level comparisons of the complete extracted text.

Each item contains:

file_a
file_b
status
hunks
added_lines
removed_lines
sample_added
sample_removed
samples_truncated


status may be:

IDENTICAL_TEXT
= the complete extracted text of the two files is identical

DIFFERENT_TEXT
= differences exist between the complete extracted text of the two files

UNAVAILABLE
= reliable text extraction was unavailable for at least one file


For DIFFERENT_TEXT:

The diff direction is always:

file_a → file_b

Therefore:

sample_added
= text lines that exist in file_b but not in file_a

sample_removed
= text lines that exist in file_a but not in file_b

added_lines
= the total number of lines added in file_b relative to file_a

removed_lines
= the total number of lines removed in file_b relative to file_a

hunks
= the approximate number of distinct difference regions in the text


Example:

{
  "file_a": "report.txt",
  "file_b": "report-v2.txt",
  "status": "DIFFERENT_TEXT",
  "added_lines": 1,
  "removed_lines": 0,
  "sample_added": [
    "okay"
  ]
}

From this evidence, you may describe:

report-v2.txt has one additional line, “okay”, compared with report.txt.

If other evidence also shows that both files belong to the same underlying content, this evidence supports VERSION.


Important:

sample_added and sample_removed contain only samples of the differences.

If:

"samples_truncated": true

this means that the actual differences exceed the displayed samples.

You must not treat the number of displayed samples as the total number of differences.

Use:

added_lines
removed_lines

for the complete counts.


If:

"text_pair_limit_reached": true

this means that because many files were selected, not every possible text-file pair was diffed.

You must not interpret the absence of a text_differences record as meaning that the files have identical text.


====================
4. HOW TO DISTINGUISH RELATIONSHIPS
====================

The only allowed relationships are:

EXACT
= the files are byte-for-byte identical

NEAR_DUPLICATE
= the main content is essentially the same, but the files were re-exported, recompressed, converted, resized, reformatted, relaid out, or otherwise processed without materially changing the main content

VERSION
= the files belong to the same underlying content and contain genuine content modifications

SAME_PROJECT
= the files are related, but their content is clearly different and they cannot reasonably be treated as versions of the same file

UNRELATED
= there is no reliable evidence that the files share a content or project relationship

MIXED
= the selected files contain multiple different relationships or independent file families

UNCERTAIN
= the current evidence is insufficient to reliably select one of the relationships above


====================
5. EXACT
====================

EXACT may only be used when the SHA-256 values are exactly identical.

You must not classify files as EXACT merely because:

- text_sha256 is identical
- filenames are identical
- file sizes are identical


====================
6. NEAR_DUPLICATE
====================

NEAR_DUPLICATE usually requires evidence showing that:

the main content is the same, but the files themselves are not completely identical.

Examples include:

- different SHA-256 values
- identical text_sha256 values
- different file formats
- different file sizes
- highly similar image pixels
- re-exporting or recompression


If the complete text is identical but the file SHA values differ:

This is a strong candidate for NEAR_DUPLICATE.

However:

If the files may contain important images, attachments, embedded objects, or other non-textual content that cannot be verified, confidence should be reduced.

You must not classify files as NEAR_DUPLICATE based only on filenames.


====================
7. VERSION
====================

VERSION requires both of the following core conditions:

A. Reliable evidence that the files belong to the same underlying content.

Possible evidence includes:

- identical normalized_family
- substantial overlap in the main body of text
- filenames with an obvious version relationship
- text diffs showing additions, deletions, or modifications to the same underlying content

and:

B. Reliable evidence that the actual content has changed.

For example:

- different text_sha256 values
- text_differences.status = DIFFERENT_TEXT
- sample_added shows newly added body text
- sample_removed shows deleted body text
- multiple diff hunks show content modifications


If two files have:

identical text, but different encoding or export methods

then they are usually better classified as:

NEAR_DUPLICATE

rather than VERSION.


If two files:

clearly share the same main content, and the complete text diff proves that text was added, deleted, or modified

then they are usually better classified as:

VERSION.


====================
8. VERSION ORDER
====================

Only populate:

version_order

when sufficient evidence exists.

The order must be:

oldest → newest


Preferred evidence includes:

1. Directionality of pairwise text diffs

Because:

in file_a → file_b

sample_added represents content added to file_b.

If file_b clearly contains additions or modifications based on file_a, and there is no evidence making the opposite direction more plausible, this may support:

file_a → file_b


2. Version markers in filenames

For example:

v1
v2
v3
revision
final

These may only be used as supporting evidence.


3. created / modified

These may only be used as further supporting evidence.


Prohibited:

Do not order versions solely by modification time.

Prohibited:

Do not assume that a file containing “final” in its name is necessarily the newest version.


If the complete version order cannot be determined reliably:

"version_order": []


If only a partial order can be determined, but all files cannot be reliably arranged:

also use:

"version_order": []

Do not guess.


====================
9. main_file
====================

Only populate a recommended main version when the evidence is sufficient.

Reasonable evidence includes:

- the version order can be reliably determined
- the file contains valid later modifications
- the content is clearly more complete
- there is actual diff evidence supporting it as a later version
- filename evidence and content evidence support each other


You must not select main_file solely because:

- its modification time is newer
- the file is larger
- its name contains final
- its name contains latest


If:

version_order can be reliably determined

and the final version does not show obvious degradation or abnormalities,

you may consider using the final version as main_file.


If the main version cannot be determined reliably:

"main_file": null


====================
10. differences
====================

differences should primarily be generated from:

local_evidence.text_differences


For example:

sample_added:
"okay"

may be described as:

"AppleScript Finder Error Log copy.txt adds the line “okay” at the end compared with AppleScript Finder Error Log.txt"


If:

added_lines = 10
removed_lines = 3

but only some samples are shown,

you may summarize:

"file_b contains multiple text changes compared with file_a, including 10 added lines and 3 removed lines"


You must not invent:

- chapters
- page-count changes
- charts
- paragraph content
- deleted content
- added content

unless explicitly supported by the evidence.


If there is insufficient evidence to describe specific differences:

"differences": []


====================
11. IMAGES
====================

For images, judgments should consider:

- SHA-256
- resolution
- format
- file size
- image_differences


image_differences.score:

The closer the score is to 0, the more visually similar the images usually are.

However, this is heuristic evidence.

You must not classify files as EXACT based on score alone.


If:

"image_pair_limit_reached": true

this means that not all image pairs were compared.

You must not interpret the absence of a score for an image pair as evidence that the images are different.


====================
12. MULTIPLE FILES AND GROUPING
====================

If all files belong to the same file family:

they may usually be placed in one group.


If multiple clearly independent file families exist:

overall_relation must be:

MIXED


groups must cover all input files.

The same file must not appear in multiple groups without a valid reason.


If the relationship within a group cannot itself be determined:

use:

UNCERTAIN

for that group’s relation.


====================
13. CONFIDENCE
====================

HIGH:

There is direct and mutually supporting local evidence.

Examples:

- SHA-256
- complete-text SHA
- clear text diff
- image-difference evidence


MEDIUM:

There are multiple pieces of supporting evidence, but some uncertainty remains.


LOW:

The judgment mainly relies on weak evidence such as:

- filenames
- timestamps
- limited excerpts

or key content could not be extracted.


====================
14. OUTPUT FORMAT
====================

You must output exactly one valid JSON object and nothing else.

Do not output:

- Markdown
- ```json
- code blocks
- text before the JSON
- text after the JSON
- titles
- comments
- reasoning
- undefined fields


All fields must always be present.

The field order must remain exactly as follows.


Strictly use:

{
  "overall_relation": "EXACT | NEAR_DUPLICATE | VERSION | SAME_PROJECT | UNRELATED | MIXED | UNCERTAIN",
  "confidence": "HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW",
  "main_file": "filename or null",
  "version_order": [
    "filenames from oldest to newest"
  ],
  "groups": [
    {
      "files": [
        "filename"
      ],
      "relation": "EXACT | NEAR_DUPLICATE | VERSION | SAME_PROJECT | UNRELATED | UNCERTAIN",
      "main_file": "filename or null",
      "version_order": [
        "filenames from oldest to newest"
      ],
      "differences": [
        "concise description of one major difference"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "summary": "concise summary in $language$",
  "recommendation": "concise organization recommendation in $language$"
}


====================
15. STRICT OUTPUT RULES
====================

- confidence may only be HIGH, MEDIUM, or LOW.

- main_file may only be an original filename that exists in input files[].name, or null.

- version_order may only contain original filenames from the input.

- groups[].files may only contain original filenames from the input.

- groups[].main_file may only be a filename that exists within that group, or null.

- If there is no reliable version order:
  "version_order": []

- If no main version can be reliably recommended:
  "main_file": null

- If there are no reliable specific differences:
  "differences": []

- groups must cover all input files.

- summary must contain no more than 3 sentences.

- recommendation must contain no more than 2 sentences.

- Each item in differences must contain no more than 1 sentence.

- Do not use "N/A", "Unknown", or similar strings meaning “unable to determine” as placeholder values.

- Uncertainty must be represented using:
  UNCERTAIN
  null
  []

- Do not recommend automatically deleting any files.

- Do not claim that any file has already been deleted, moved, modified, or renamed.

- recommendation may only suggest that the user manually:
  keep
  inspect
  compare
  archive
  organize

- Do not explain the internal reasoning process.

- The final output must be directly parseable by a standard JSON parser.

item.title: Suggest Better Filenames on Mac with Shortcuts and Auto Filename Helper
item.description:
Auto Filename Helper is a native macOS companion that validates and applies filename suggestions supplied by a Shortcut.

A download called document (3).pdf says little about its contents. A meaningful name makes later search easier, but an automated suggestion still needs checking: it may be too vague, contain an unsafe character, or collide with another file.

Auto Filename Helper separates those jobs. The Shortcut derives the suggested name; the native app checks the request and handles the actual rename. The helper itself is not an AI model and does not inspect a document to invent its title.

Real confirmation window and public download

Figure 1 shows the actual confirmation window. The original notes.txt contains community garden volunteer meeting notes; the model proposes a dated name at 95% confidence. Because the original name is ambiguous, the helper still asks for confirmation.

Download the ready-to-import Shortcut. The editable source, scripts, and prompts ship with the MIT project. Remove or rename an older same-name Shortcut before importing. The complete workflow also requires macOS with the Use Model action, Apple Intelligence, and an available ChatGPT model; the helper’s macOS 13 minimum applies only to the native app.

Build the helper and connect the Shortcut

The project currently provides source and an included Auto Filename.shortcut, rather than a packaged GitHub Release. Building requires macOS 13 or later and Xcode Command Line Tools.

Download the repository, inspect its installation script, then run:

1

./build_and_install.sh

The script installs ~/Applications/AutoFilenameHelper.app. Import Auto Filename.shortcut into Shortcuts. The public download already calls the default installation through $HOME; no username replacement is needed.

This connection matters. Merely opening the app does not create a filename suggestion; the Shortcut must send the selected path and analysis result to the helper.

Think of it as a handoff with a checkpoint: select a file such as document (3).pdf in Finder, let the Shortcut propose a descriptive name, and let the helper check the path, extension, and possible conflict. A proposal such as “project meeting notes.pdf” is only an example; the real name depends on what the Shortcut derives from your file.

Try one file before a batch

Start with a disposable copy of a supported file. Run the Shortcut from Finder, inspect the suggested filename and reason, and check the result in Finder.

The helper receives fields including the path, suggestion, confidence, and reason. It validates the request, preserves the original extension by default, and uses moves that do not overwrite an existing file. It rejects unsafe or hidden names, symlinks, unsupported file types, and unchanged names.

Those checks protect the rename operation; they do not prove that the proposed title describes the contents accurately. Keep names factual and easy to recognize later.

Decide when confirmation is required

The app’s settings include a rename threshold, extension handling, conflict behaviour, appearance, and English/Chinese interface choices. Ambiguous names, low-confidence suggestions, executables, and disabled automatic renaming can trigger confirmation.

Quick Look, Reveal in Finder, and Copy Path help inspect the original before accepting. For files with uncertain contents, the right answer may simply be to keep the existing name until you have checked it.

On the first run, use a copy and check three things: whether the proposed name really describes the content, whether .pdf or another extension stays intact, and whether the folder already contains that name. Even a high confidence value is a reason to inspect the file, not a substitute for opening it.

A confidence value is supplied by the workflow, not an independent certification from the helper. Moving the threshold should be a deliberate convenience choice, especially when filenames influence your later search or filing rules.

Find the project folder before building

If you use Code → Download ZIP on GitHub, unzip the archive and locate the folder containing build_and_install.sh. That is the folder Terminal needs as its current directory. Type cd , drag the folder into Terminal, and press Return before running the build command. This also handles spaces in the path.

If the script reports missing Xcode Command Line Tools, run xcode-select --install, complete the system installer, then return to the project. The script rebuilds and replaces ~/Applications/AutoFilenameHelper.app. Keep a copy first if you have customized an existing installation. The source folder is useful for future updates, while the Shortcut should call the executable inside the installed app.

In the Shortcut editor, find the shell action that invokes the helper and preserve the preceding analysis actions. The supplied replacement script handles the handoff; it does not create a missing analysis workflow. If you choose a different app location, update that invocation too. Otherwise a suggested name may exist while the Shortcut cannot find the program that applies it.

Choose a naming convention you can keep using

Think about the words you will search for later. For meeting documents, a project, topic, and a date actually present in the document can be useful. For invoices, the supplier or invoice number may matter more. A polished title that invents a year, person, or version is harder to trust than a modest, accurate description.

Renaming document (3).pdf to quarterly budget discussion.pdf helps if “budget” is what you will remember. If that name already exists, inspect both documents rather than relying on a numbered suffix to explain their relationship. Keeping the extension is sensible: changing .pdf to .docx does not convert a PDF into a Word document.

Try several copies before choosing a threshold: a clearly named file, an ambiguous one, and a case that conflicts with an existing name. Watch which suggestions are accepted, questioned, or rejected. This gives the threshold a practical meaning in your own workflow instead of treating it as an abstract accuracy score.

When the Shortcut runs but the name stays unchanged

Follow the chain: selected file, generated suggestion, handoff, then rename. If only Settings opens, check whether the Shortcut is passing the payload to standard input. If a confirmation window appears, it may still be waiting for your decision. If the helper reports an unchanged name or unsupported type, resolve that message before rerunning the same input.

Always verify the path. A similarly named document in Downloads, on the Desktop, and in a cloud folder can be three separate files. Use Reveal in Finder to locate the intended original, then check that folder after the rename. If a script or project configuration refers to the old filename, account for those references before changing it.

Local renaming and upstream analysis are separate

The helper makes no network requests. The Shortcut is responsible for deriving the suggestion and may use an AI service depending on its actions and configuration.

Review that Shortcut before applying it to personal documents. “The rename happens locally” does not automatically mean the whole analysis workflow stays on the Mac.

For an explanation of an unfamiliar file before renaming it, see What File Is This. To find the renamed item later, MacHunt provides local filename search. Setup details remain in the project README.

Key Shortcut scripts and prompts

These scripts and prompts match the public source: classify the original name, collect bounded evidence, request three labeled result lines, then validate and rename locally. The image branch also attaches the image. Both suggestion branches carry the naming instructions directly, avoiding a reference to text produced later in the workflow.

During diagnosis on November 2, 2026, the incorrect prompt reference caused the model to return a prose summary without the required fields; the app silently rejected it. After repair, the English fixture was renamed and notes.txt opened the native confirmation window. High-confidence suggestions for meaningless original names may rename automatically without a window.

[[ -n "$path" ]] || exit 0
[[ -e "$path" && ! -L "$path" ]] || exit 0

[[ -e "$path" && ! -L "$path" ]] || exit 0

modified=$(/bin/date -r "$modified_epoch" '+%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z' 2>/dev/null || print unknown)

if [[ -d "$path" ]]; then
  item_type="directory"
  case "$lower" in

  "CURRENT_FILENAME=$name" \
  "ORIGINAL_EXTENSION=$suffix" \
  "FILE_SIZE_BYTES=$size" \
  "CREATED_DATE=$created" \
  "MODIFIED_DATE=$modified"

set -u

payload=$(/bin/cat)
quality=$(printf '%s\n' "$payload" | /usr/bin/grep -Eio 'meaningless|ambiguous|meaningful' | /usr/bin/tail -1)
[[ "$quality" == "ambiguous" || "$quality" == "meaningless" ]] || exit 0

path_b64=$(printf '%s\n' "$payload" | /usr/bin/sed -n 's/^PATH_B64=//p' | /usr/bin/head -1)
[[ -n "$path_b64" ]] || exit 0
path=$(printf '%s' "$path_b64" | /usr/bin/base64 -D 2>/dev/null) || exit 0
[[ -e "$path" && ! -L "$path" ]] || exit 0
[[ -f "$path" || -d "$path" ]] || exit 0

if [[ -d "$path" ]]; then
  item_type="directory"
else
  item_type="file"
fi

name="${path:t}"
lower="${name:l}"
size=$(/usr/bin/stat -f '%z' "$path" 2>/dev/null || print 0)
mime=$(/usr/bin/file -b --mime-type "$path" 2>/dev/null || print unknown)
description=$(/usr/bin/file -b "$path" 2>/dev/null || print unknown)

mode=TEXT
case "$mime" in image/*) (( size <= 52428800 )) && mode=IMAGE ;; esac

print 'STATE=EVIDENCE_READY'
print "ITEM_TYPE=$item_type"
print "ANALYSIS_MODE=$mode"
print "INITIAL_QUALITY=$quality"
print "PATH_B64=$path_b64"
print "CURRENT_FILENAME=$name"
print "FILE_SIZE_BYTES=$size"
print "MIME_TYPE=$mime"
print "FILE_DESCRIPTION=$description"

print '\n--- SPOTLIGHT METADATA ---'
/usr/bin/mdls \
  -name kMDItemWhereFroms \
  -name kMDItemContentType \
  -name kMDItemKind \
  -name kMDItemTitle \
  -name kMDItemVersion \
  -name kMDItemAuthors \
  -name kMDItemDownloadedDate \
  -name kMDItemCFBundleIdentifier \
  -name kMDItemDurationSeconds \
  -name kMDItemPixelHeight \
  -name kMDItemPixelWidth \
  -name kMDItemAudioBitRate \
  -name kMDItemCodecs \
  "$path" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -c 20000

print '\n\n--- EXTENDED ATTRIBUTE NAMES ---'
/usr/bin/xattr "$path" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -100
print '\n--- QUARANTINE ATTRIBUTE (bounded) ---'
/usr/bin/xattr -p com.apple.quarantine "$path" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -c 4096

if [[ "$item_type" == "directory" ]]; then
  print '\n\n--- DIRECTORY CONTENTS (top level only) ---'
  /bin/ls -1A "$path" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -200 | /usr/bin/head -c 20000
  exit 0
fi

case "$lower" in
  *.zip)
    print '\n\n--- ARCHIVE DIRECTORY LISTING (no extraction) ---'
    /usr/bin/unzip -Z1 "$path" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -200 | /usr/bin/head -c 20000
    ;;
  *.tar|*.tar.gz|*.tgz|*.tar.bz2|*.tar.xz)
    print '\n\n--- ARCHIVE DIRECTORY LISTING (no extraction) ---'
    /usr/bin/tar -tf "$path" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -200 | /usr/bin/head -c 20000
    ;;
  *.gz|*.bz2|*.xz)
    print '\n\n--- COMPRESSED FILE SUMMARY (no extraction) ---'
    case "$lower" in
      *.gz) /usr/bin/gzip -l "$path" 2>/dev/null ;;
      *) print 'The built-in tools identify this compressed stream; contents were not expanded.' ;;
    esac
    ;;
  *.docx|*.pptx|*.xlsx)
    print '\n\n--- OFFICE CORE PROPERTIES ---'
    /usr/bin/unzip -p "$path" docProps/core.xml 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -c 10000 | /usr/bin/sed 's/<[^>]*>/ /g'
    print '\n--- OFFICE CONTENT SAMPLE ---'
    case "$lower" in
      *.docx) entry='word/document.xml' ;;
      *.pptx) entry=$(/usr/bin/unzip -Z1 "$path" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/grep '^ppt/slides/slide[0-9].*\.xml$' | /usr/bin/head -1) ;;
      *.xlsx) entry='xl/sharedStrings.xml' ;;
    esac
    [[ -n "${entry-}" ]] && /usr/bin/unzip -p "$path" "$entry" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -c 24000 | /usr/bin/sed 's/<[^>]*>/ /g'
    ;;
  *.pdf)
    print '\n\n--- SPOTLIGHT TEXT SAMPLE ---'
    /usr/bin/mdls -raw -name kMDItemTextContent "$path" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -c 24000
    ;;
  *.dmg)
    print '\n\n--- DISK IMAGE INFO (not mounted) ---'
    /usr/bin/hdiutil imageinfo "$path" 2>/dev/null | /usr/bin/head -c 16000
    print '\n--- SIGNATURE ASSESSMENT (not executed) ---'
    /usr/sbin/spctl -a -vv -t open --context context:primary-signature "$path" 2>&1 | /usr/bin/head -c 8000
    ;;
  *.pkg)
    print '\n\n--- INSTALLER SIGNATURE (not installed) ---'
